data.why: qPilot's own public demo study (Vermeulen 2009/Ruijter 2013, CC BY 4.0, SHA-256 pinned) is pre-fetched during install so 'Open the demo study' works offline; two small real instrument fixtures from the repo's own test corpus (a raw RDML curve file and a Cq-only Excel table) are also handed to the browser to exercise the 'upload your own file' path.

goals: Load raw qPCR instrument curves (RDML or a vendor export) and get them correctly recognised, with the curve calls and amplification quality checked before any result is shown
Confirm the experimental design (targets, groups, control genes, the comparison) so a fold-change analysis can run
See each gene's fold-change call, its confidence, and which analysis choices (threshold, control-gene set, empty-well rule) could flip the conclusion
Check plate controls (NTCs, melt curves, standards) and trace a surprising result back to the specific well driving it
Run the robustness audit across many reasonable analysis combinations to see how often each gene's call holds
Export the results (Excel/CSV/figures or a GraphPad Prism project) and a hash-chained Analysis Record documenting every decision

review.summary: The goal and phases match what the README says qPilot is for: a blind design and curve review, then Decision Cards and a robustness map showing which choices flip each gene's call, then a Prism export and a hash-chained record. The features are well cut, and the later Results, Controls, Prism and Record screens back up their nodes. But the Design and Curves tasks cite overwritten screens that don't show what they claim. The replay couldn't get past Design, so t3–t12 aren't independently confirmed, and the audit verdicts, Trace, own-data intake and standard exports are missing, so this needs fixes before filing.
